proposed.text: A building is provided with an automatic sprinkler system throughout. By how much does this extend the allowable travel distance to the nearest exit compared to a non-sprinklered building?

options.text: The travel distance increases from 30 meters to 45 meters
The travel distance increases from 45 meters to 60 meters
The travel distance increases from 60 meters to 75 meters
The travel distance increases from 45 meters to 90 meters

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Under Sec. 1207 read together with Sec. 1212, the allowable travel distance without sprinklers is 45m. Full sprinkler coverage extends this to 60m, a 33% increase reflecting the additional evacuation time sprinklers provide.
proposed.explanation: Sprinklers allow the 45m→60m travel distance extension because they suppress or control a fire, buying occupants additional safe evacuation time. This trade-off is frequently used in large open-plan offices or shopping centers where placing exits at 45m intervals would be architecturally disruptive.
proposed.code_citation: PD 1096, Rule XII, Sec. 1207 and Sec. 1212
